title: Anywhere it fits
lede: Callers name a job, not a machine.
why: Hard-coding hosts means idle cards beside overloaded ones. A lease names a target and the grant returns the address, so placement can change without touching a single caller.

beats.title: The first choice gets the work
beats.text: A chat request names a model, not a machine. Both small cards have qwen3:8b on disk, so configuration order decides: the RTX 4060.

beats.title: Same model, second machine
beats.text: A second job asks for the same model. The RTX 4060 is already serving one lease, so this one goes to the GTX 1070 Ti: loading a model takes seconds, waiting behind a job can take minutes.

beats.title: No room here, so it spills
beats.text: Speech normally runs on the RTX 4060, but a lease is using that card. echo-xtts on the RTX 3090 declares that it serves the same target, so the grant comes back with its address: http://rtx3090:8141. The caller never had to know.

beats.title: Three cards, one queue
beats.text: Three callers, three different GPUs, and none of them picked a host.
